title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 346
paragraphs: Some, however, tell the following tale about this cow and the colossal statues — that Mykerinos fell in love with his own daughter and afterwards raped her; whereupon, they say, the girl strangled herself in grief, and he buried her in this cow; and her mother cut off the hands of the maids who had betrayed the daughter to her father — which is why the images of them have suffered the very thing the maids suffered in their lifetime. In saying this they speak foolishly, as it seems to me, especially with regard to the hands of the statues. For we ourselves saw that their hands had dropped off through the lapse of time, and they were still to be seen lying at their feet even down to my own day.
